headline: Wall thickness is not a cost or mass driver for a coilgun. There is no chamber pressure; the only structural load is magnetic pressure of 34 MPa on the coil, which S-glass banding carries at 0.93 mm and 0.33 kg over all 31 stages. Total structure is 1.7 kg against 28 kg of capacitors.

recommended.bore_tube: G10/FR4 or PEEK, 1.5 mm wall, MUST be insulating
recommended.outer_case: Ti-6Al-4V or Al, 0.8 mm minimum gauge (not strength-limited)

for_cost_model: Model launcher mass as: capacitors (E_stored/1500 J/kg) + copper (~4 kg) + 1.3x integration factor. Treat all walls as a fixed ~1.5 kg. Do not optimise wall thickness -- it is 4% of the mass and its cost is negligible against the capacitor bank.
trap: The bore tube must be electrically insulating. A metal tube is a shorted turn around the armature: it carries induced current, shields the armature and destroys the coupling. This is the one structural choice that can break the launcher.
